AW-STUDY-0027

Brute Fight

Two epic heroes from Meshy, cleaned up the Bruiser way, painted, rigged on one shared skeleton and given a fighting move set. Every blow has a matching hit and blocked reaction. It's a cartoon brawl in a ranch ring: stars, dust and bonks, never blood. This is the start of a street fighter.

FightWatch every move

The fight starts with the brutes fighting each other on their own. Press a key or touch the screen and you take over the red one. On a keyboard, A and D walk, W jumps, S blocks, J jabs, K throws a heavy, L throws an uppercut and I swings the two-fisted hammer. On a phone, drag on the left to walk (flick up to jump) and use the fists on the right; the crossed arms block.

His pictures, and the painted fighters

Spin either fighter. Meshy gave both of them back plain grey, so the paint is ours: each face of the full 30,000-face Meshy mesh gets a role (skin, tank top, shorts, brows) from the learned body rings, and the colours and shadows are baked down onto the 3,000-face fighter with a warm top light, tinted shadows and a little brush grain.

Also on the same skeleton: idle, walk_fwd, walk_back, jump, block, hurt, hit_axe (crushed to one knee, for a hammer that lands while standing), fall, getup and victory (a double-biceps flex). 19 clips per fighter, and both fighters share every clip.

Every clip, frame by frame

How the world shows the fight

  • The ring bell on its post rings in each round and rings it out. Everyone in the ring hears it, so it's in the world.
  • A tired brute sways slower and lower in his guard, so the other brute (and you) can read it.
  • A hit throws a star burst and a bonk, a block throws a blue ring and a clack, and a landing kicks up dust. The screen gives a small shake. These are presentation-layer cues that the brutes can't perceive.
  • The only overlay is two strength pills at the top, with no words. On a phone the move pad sits in the bottom-right corner, all inside the 8% budget.

How it's built

  1. Meshy made both heroes from his pictures (tasks 01a167ca and 01a16806, made in the Bruiser study, so no new credits were spent).
  2. Cleanup, the Bruiser way: weld Meshy's seams, cut the hero into rings per named part (tools/bruiser-study/scale), and decimate to about 3,000 faces.
  3. Paint: give each hero face a role from the rings, then bake colour, ambient occlusion and height from the 30,000-face hero onto fresh UVs on the low mesh, and combine them into one painted texture.
  4. Rig: 20 bones placed from the learned rings, at fixed fractions of each part. Weights come from the part each vertex belongs to and its distance to that part's bones; fists that hang by the hips are claimed for the arm.
  5. Moves: key poses written as numbers in tools/brute-fight/moves.py, about the body's own axes, become glTF animations. Game data (when each blow lands, its reach and its reactions) ships next to them as moves.json.

One command rebuilds both fighters: python3 tools/brute-fight/build.py --sheet (about 20 seconds each). A new brute only needs a Meshy model, its learned rings and a paint line in fighters.json.
